name: Learn basic parkour landings
blurb: The most valuable part of parkour for everyone, including people who will never vault anything: how to absorb a drop without wrecking your knees.
gear: A low step, then a low wall
steps: Learn the landing shape on the spot: land on the balls of the feet, hips back, knees tracking over toes, absorbing quietly.
Practise the two-foot landing from a low step, aiming for silence. Noise means you absorbed with your skeleton rather than your muscles.
Progress the height in small increments over weeks — the tissue adaptation is slower than the skill.
Learn to convert forward momentum into a roll rather than a hard stop.
Learn the precision landing: land on a defined edge, balanced and still.
Build ankle and knee strength deliberately with calf raises and step-downs.
tips: Knees collapsing inwards is the injury pattern to watch for. Film yourself from the front.
Progress in height slowly. Impact tolerance builds far more slowly than confidence.
proof: Silent, controlled landings from waist height, ten in a row, with good knee alignment on video.
